definition: Difficult to control, manage, or solve.
example: The team confronted an intractable software defect.
nuance: Intractable can describe people, conditions, or problems.
options: The intractable dispute resisted every proposed compromise.
The intractable dispute was easily settled in seconds.
The problem was intractable because everyone readily agreed.
Intractable meant the dispute had never begun.
reasons: Resistance to resolution illustrates an intractable problem.
Ready agreement does not illustrate resistance.
